source_user: Write a small, dependency-light Python implementation for latency percentiles. Variant 6. Contract: Compute p50 and p99 from request latencies, define the interpolation method, and handle an empty input explicitly. Include tests for boundary cases and a brief complexity analysis.
source_assistant: Provide typed or clearly documented code, input validation, deterministic tests, and explicit assumptions. Contract to satisfy: Compute p50 and p99 from request latencies, define the interpolation method, and handle an empty input explicitly.
corrected_answer: Implement a dependency-light percentile helper that materializes the iterable once, rejects empty input explicitly (for example, ValueError), and validates every latency as a finite, nonnegative real number while excluding bool; document the latency unit and whether values are milliseconds, microseconds, or another agreed unit. Sort a copy so caller input is not mutated. Use and state one quantile convention: linear interpolation with position q*(n-1), lower=floor(position), upper=ceil(position), and weighted interpolation; require q in [0,1]. Return p50 and p99 using q=0.50 and q=0.99 under that convention, noting that for one value both equal it and for two values p50 is the midpoint and p99 is close to the larger endpoint. Materialize only once if given a generator. Deterministic tests must cover empty, one-item, two-item, unsorted, duplicate, endpoint, exact-interpolation, invalid negative/non-finite/bool/type, input-preservation, and p99-precision cases, plus both named percentile outputs. State O(n log n) time and O(n) auxiliary space for sorting. Do not claim the chosen interpolation is a universal production standard; require evidence for the service metric convention, units, precision/overflow policy, streaming or very-large-input behavior, and whether negative latencies are ever meaningful.

Latency units, clock source, aggregation scope, outliers, and sampling policy are unspecified and can invalidate interpretation.
Sorting costs O(n log n) time and O(n) extra memory; very large or streaming workloads need a separate design.
Floating-point precision and overflow behavior for extreme values require explicit policy and tests.
Synthetic calibration is provisional and does not establish production correctness or domain authority.
evidence_required: Confirm the production percentile/interpolation convention and expected p50/p99 semantics against the consuming system.
Confirm latency units, clock/measurement boundaries, filtering, sampling, and aggregation policy.
Benchmark memory/time and define an evidence-backed strategy for streaming or very-large inputs.
Test numerical precision and extreme-value behavior on the supported Python/runtime versions.
